The Nov 4 morning bounce (SPY +1.27%, VIX -11.14% to 18.51) is intraday and unconfirmed at the close.
reaction.invalidation: A held close above SPX 7,820 / SMH 600 with VIX below 18 and HY OAS still calm proves the correction call wrong and voids this ladder; conversely a credit crack (HY OAS above 4%) voids the probe-and-wait ladder and forces stand-down.

ladder.response: Prepare Tranche A only: require the tally to reach at least 3 of 4 (volume climax plus VIX rollover) before any deployment — a zone print alone is not a buy.
Treat as the trap case confirmed: no chasing, hold cash, expect a second low; the retest verdict decides the next entry, not the rally.

ladder.response: Stand down: all deployment triggers void, reassess the regime — the correction has become a regime break.

ladder.response: Re-entry confirmed: the episode is over (first case) or the bottom is verified (second case) — stance moves from Watch to Add on the pre-committed plan.

reaction.trapRisk: The Nov 4 bounce is the classic first bounce inside a correction: SPY +1.27% and VIX -11.14% to 18.51 look like relief, but the tally is still 2 of 4, VIX has not rolled over from its 5-day high of 21.15, and SMH is still 9.19% below its 50-day. Entries that chase this bounce buy the top of the failure-zone retest. No new entries until the bounce either clears the failure zone or fails and produces a second low that holds.

strategyPosture: Watch. The correction is intact through the Nov 3 close (SPX -3.51% from its high, SMH -22.82%, tally 2 of 4) and this morning's bounce is unconfirmed. Hold existing positions; no new adds until a Zone 2 print or a tally confirmation arrives.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read and the data agree, which is the point: an index down 3.5% from its high with calm credit is not a rollover, but the divergence itself is real and worth tracking. If credit flips — lending standards tightening toward stress or HY OAS breaking above 4% — the rotation story dies and the rollover story takes over. Until then, the Mag7 drawdown is a leadership rotation to trade around, not a market to exit.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average -15.84% from their 52-week highs against SPY at only -3.5%, a -12.34-point divergence gap; the weakest Mag7 name, GOOGL, is -31.5% from its high while the strongest, MSFT, is only -5.5% back. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.43% and calm. The weakness is concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight, not in credit or in the broad index.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as an AI crash: the Magnificent 7 are down hard and the month's laggards are a who's-who of the AI complex. The fear is that index leadership is rolling over into a broad market break.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS closing above 4% or SLOOS moving toward the ~40% stress threshold, either of which voids the rotation read.

themes.counterRead: Price and fundamentals are moving in opposite directions across the whole complex — the classic dislocation setup, and the reason the opportunity list is long. But multiple compression can persist while the correction runs: the same names are still 15-48% below their highs for a reason, and GOOGL at RSI 22.2 shows how far oversold can go before it turns. This is a watchlist to verify name by name, not a buy signal — the entry gate is the episode state, not the discount.

themes.label: AI infrastructure: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: The market believes the AI buildout is over-earning and over-supplied: semis and AI software have fallen 15-48% from their highs in a month, and the story now is derating, not growth.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing inside Zone 2 ($470-505) with the capitulation tally reaching at least 3 of 4 before any name graduates from watchlist to entry.

themes.counterRead: The correction has brought the power leg back toward a story that still has structural legs — data-center power demand has not gone away — but the near-term revenue read on VST is deteriorating, so this is not a clean fundamentals-ahead-of-price setup. Insider buying at the trough argues the drawdown is sentiment, not thesis death; deteriorating revenue argues the trough may not be in. Both can be true at once, which is why this theme stays ALIGNED and on the watchlist rather than promoted.
themes.dataAnchor: VST is -29.1% from its 52-week high and -12.28% over the past month; SMR is -30.34% over the month; OKLO is -35.92% over the month; CCJ is -17.2% over the month; GEV is -12.97% over the month. The declines are flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN across the group. The one hard counter-signal inside the group is VST itself: insiders bought $1.17M at the trough, even as its revenue inflection reads DETERIORATING.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the correction hits the power leg
themes.narrative: Nuclear power for AI data centers was one of the year's consensus trades; the narrative now is that the power leg was the most stretched part of the AI stack and is giving it all back.
themes.watchFor: VST revenue inflection flipping from DETERIORATING to RECOVERY, or a second insider-buying print at lower prices.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree that the hurdle is higher, not that the trade is dead: 'higher hurdle, not extinction' is exactly what the price action shows — NVDA in Zone 1, not in freefall, and the index only -3.51% from its high. The risk is that a hawkish December FOMC turns a higher hurdle into a higher discount rate for the whole complex; the offset is that a sweep that favors software as defensive could rotate money inside tech rather than out of it.
themes.dataAnchor: The midterm election is an active event with 19 matched headlines, including a Democratic sweep framing software as a defensive play and AI facing 'a higher hurdle, not an extinction event'. The December FOMC is an anticipated HIGH-signal event with headlines on the Fed signaling higher rates. Rates confirm the hawkish read: the 10-year is 4.91%, the 2-year 4.59%, the 30-year 5.28%, the curve +0.32, and the real 10-year 2.61%. At the same time NVDA retook the world's-biggest-company title on Election Day and closed Nov 3 up 2.29% at $206.69.
themes.label: Policy overhang: midterms and a hawkish Fed
themes.narrative: The market believes politics just raised the hurdle for AI: a Democratic midterm sweep puts software in a defensive frame and AI faces a higher regulatory and spending hurdle, while the Fed keeps signaling higher rates into the December 8-9 FOMC.
themes.watchFor: December FOMC language on Dec 8-9 and the 10-year closing above 5.0%, either of which reprices the AI complex lower regardless of earnings.

themes.counterRead: A first bounce inside a correction is the most dangerous price action to chase: it looks like a bottom and usually isn't one. The narrative that the low is in is ahead of the data — nothing in the episode block confirms capitulation yet. If the bounce holds and clears the failure zone, the story changes; if it fails there, it becomes the trap that defines the next leg down. Either verdict comes from the close, not the morning.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce is real but unconfirmed at the close. The mechanical capitulation tally is still 2 of 4: zone occupancy and credit calm are confirmed, but there is no volume climax (SMH volume 0.92x its 20-day average, close in 33% of its range) and no VIX rollover (VIX 20.83 at the Nov 3 close, 5-day high 21.15). SMH is still -9.19% below its 50-day and -22.82% from its high; the month's laggards are still -26% to -44% over one month (TQQQ -26.42%, SMR -30.34%, OKLO -35.92%, CONL -44.45%) despite today's bounce.
themes.label: The bounce is a test, not a bottom
